assertion_analysis: Lines 65-70: restoring the refusal-only predicate makes the timed-out/unreachable read return no head or only one attempt, failing the expected independently stubbed SHA, attempt count, route order and returned route checks.
Lines 109-112: readiness checks fail if the child never imports or imports a different source tree; these compare distinct processes, not a value merely echoed by the product.

Lines 120-132: restoring an unbounded runner makes communicate exceed three seconds after readiness and fail after proving the requested stub operation started; wrong timeout translation fails child status, on_branch, cause or detail assertions.

Lines 145-148: omitting timeout or connect options fails concrete timeout/routing assertions; replacing the caller GIT_SSH_COMMAND loses the independently supplied key and fails prefix preservation, but core.sshCommand and GIT_SSH are untested.
Lines 153-154: indiscriminate fallback on any port-22 or timeout error fails the authentication-error or port-443 negative cases.
Lines 174-179: restoring refusal-only fallback makes timed-out/no-route fetch report unreachable, with one fetch rather than two and no 443 second attempt.
No added product assertion compares an output only to the same value supplied as its expected input; the read SHA comes from a separate executable transport stub.

findings.text: blocking: when GIT_SSH_COMMAND is absent, setting it to plain ssh plus ConnectTimeout overrides both repository core.sshCommand and GIT_SSH, discarding configured identity/proxy/wrapper commands; reads and fetches that worked before can now fail authentication or connectivity, and a push using core.sshCommand can succeed while its confirmation uses a different transport; preserve the effective configured command and add regression coverage for these paths.
